headline: A year-long Senate investigation led by Democratic senators argues that some big tech companies are misleading the public about the costs and benefits of AI data centers.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 7: new exclusive report on 8 Oct 2026; findings come from one party's senators and the companies dispute parts of them.
importance_line: Households and local governments weighing data center deals gain new evidence on who pays for power and tax breaks, as Congress looks at possible rules, but the report comes from Democratic senators' staff and the companies dispute parts of it.
summary: TIME reports, in an exclusive, that the investigation by Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren, Chris Van Hollen and Richard Blumenthal into seven data center developers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix) found that several refused to give full permanent job figures and that none would agree to pay for new power infrastructure their data centers made necessary. The companies say they pay the direct costs of serving their sites but that wider grid upgrades also benefit other customers, and Meta disputes that its Louisiana project is driving up local electric bills.
notes: Read the full TIME article. Report is from Democratic senators' offices.
